SMTO-CTX-0011 — SMTO asked for too small a piece of an attached file

GUID: a6e3548f-4e1b-4b13-bd83-9e5afbf790e4
Slug: context-read-byte-limit-too-small
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • While reading a file you attached, SMTO asked for a piece so small it couldn't hold even one whole letter, so it got nothing back. The file itself is fine and unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going for a step or two. SMTO sees this message and usually asks again for a sensible amount.
  2. If it repeats, open Agent Checks in the message box and, under Context & Attachments, turn on Read full attached context. With full reading on, SMTO ignores the tiny size and reads the rest of the file.
  3. Then tell SMTO in the conversation: "Read the attached file again without a byte limit." This points it back at the file with a request it can fulfil.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next steps show text from the attached file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't attach the same file many more times; the file isn't the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A read_context call using the deprecated byte limit cut off before the next complete character, returning an empty page although source text remains (byte_limit_too_small).

What this means

  • The deprecated byte limit cuts off the next UTF-8 character entirely, leaving an empty page despite remaining source text. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The deprecated byte limit cuts off the next UTF-8 character entirely, leaving an empty page despite remaining source text.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the byte allowance with the next character boundary; a character count avoids this byte-versus-character mismatch.

How to fix it

  • Use max_characters instead of the deprecated limit argument, or pass a limit large enough for the next complete character in the selected encoding (native/context_reads.py read_source). Enabling read_full_attached_context also bypasses the byte limit.
  • Use max_characters instead of the deprecated byte limit, or allow enough bytes for the next complete character.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The page contains at least one whole character and returns a valid continuation cursor.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
